summary: T10 trimmed the eframe feature set and closed R2's T10 findings. The egui-ui gate in docs/architecture/verification.md (full gate plus the src/ui2/ scoped-loop row) and the Settings UI tests step in .github/workflows/rust-tests.yml now select tests/ui_semantic, so the label-driven tests run in both the standing gate and CI; before this change they only ran when someone repeated T8's explicit command. eframe now uses default-features = false with accesskit, default_fonts and wgpu: the Windows egui-ui graph drops 37 crates (232 -> 195) and Cargo.lock loses 42 package entries, while the app still builds, launches, and exposes its 9-node UI Automation tree. The full gate passes and the default dependency tree stays GUI-free. Rework round 2: README.md §Tests was still showing the pre-round egui-ui commands, so it now matches the gate (--test ui_semantic on the test line, --all-targets on the clippy line).

feature_evaluation.spec: EGUI_MIGRATION.md T10: try `default-features = false` on eframe with the minimum set for a Windows wgpu build, keep whatever actually compiles and runs.

retained.why: Load-bearing and verified negatively: with accesskit removed the crate still compiles and the window still opens, but the UIA tree exposes 0 controls (measured), which is exactly the Iced defect the migration exists to fix. With it, the same build exposes 9 nodes / 4 buttons.

The renderer. eframe's Renderer::default has a compile_error! when neither glow nor wgpu is enabled (eframe 0.36.2 src/epi.rs:601-605), and `wgpu_no_default_features` alone would leave no backend because `dx12` arrives with wgpu's own default set (wgpu 30.0.1 Cargo.toml `default = [std, parking_lot, dx12, metal, gles, vulkan, wgsl, webgpu]`).

Supplies the text faces. Kept explicitly even though it is currently reachable transitively (egui is a direct dependency with its default features, so egui/default_fonts -> epaint/default_fonts would enable it anyway); pinning it states the requirement instead of relying on another crate's defaults.

dropped.why: Not in eframe's defaults; the wgpu path is the one this app uses. Its absence also removes egui_glow, glutin, glutin-winit, cgl and the glutin_egl_sys/glutin_glx_sys bindings from the lock.
Adds hyperlink handling via egui-winit/links -> webbrowser -> url -> idna -> icu_*. The UI contains no hyperlink, open_url or Hyperlink usage (grep over src/ui2 and src/bin).
Linux-only backend for a dependency declared under cfg(windows); never built here.
Linux-only backend for a dependency declared under cfg(windows); never built here.
wasm-only (web-sys SpeechSynthesis); not a target this crate builds.

Re-adds winit's Linux-only defaults (x11, wayland, wayland-dlopen, wayland-csd-adwaita). winit still receives rwh_06 from eframe's own explicit `features = ["rwh_06"]`, so the Windows backend and raw-window-handle support are unaffected.

feature_evaluation.measured_effect: egui-ui normal graph 232 -> 195 packages (37 fewer). Cargo.lock loses 42 package entries (449 lines): the links chain (webbrowser, url, idna, idna_adapter, form_urlencoded, percent-encoding, icu_collections, icu_locale_core, icu_normalizer, icu_normalizer_data, icu_properties, icu_properties_data, icu_provider, litemap, potential_utf, tinystr, writeable, yoke, yoke-derive, zerofrom, zerofrom-derive, zerotrie, zerovec, zerovec-derive, displaydoc, synstructure, stable_deref_trait, utf8_iter), the glow/glutin renderer (egui_glow, glutin, glutin-winit, glutin_egl_sys, glutin_glx_sys, cgl), and the sctk-adwaita wayland decoration chain (sctk-adwaita, tiny-skia, tiny-skia-path, ab_glyph, ab_glyph_rasterizer, owned_ttf_parser, ttf-parser, strict-num, arrayref).
feature_evaluation.lock_regenerated: Cargo.lock is part of this change and is required, not incidental: with the pre-change lock in place `cargo check --locked --no-default-features --features egui-ui --all-targets` fails with 'cannot update the lock file ... because --locked was passed to prevent this'. It was regenerated by a non---locked check and the --locked run then passes.

risks: The eframe feature trim is verified on Windows only. It is a cfg(windows) dependency and the gate's Linux check never enables egui-ui, so a future cross-platform settings build would need its own feature list (x11/wayland/winit-default would come back); nothing in the gate covers that today.

docs/architecture/ui.md still describes the Iced UI (lines 44-47 name `iced-ui`, `lyon` and the src/ui/ owners, line 216 refers to iced-ui in build.rs). That file is T11's scope ('update docs/architecture/ui.md ... where they name Iced'), so it was not touched; the gate itself contains no stale iced-ui command.

The default_fonts feature is currently redundant (egui's own defaults already enable egui/default_fonts for the direct egui dependency). It is kept explicit deliberately; if egui is later switched to default-features = false without adding default_fonts here, text rendering breaks.

Removing the glow capability means eframe can no longer fall back to a GL renderer if wgpu fails to initialise on a given machine. This matches the pre-existing configuration (glow was never enabled) but is now explicit rather than incidental.

Native visual acceptance remains uncovered per docs/architecture/verification.md Unverified Areas. The app's window, liveness and UIA tree were verified programmatically here; no pixel-level or rendered-text check was performed, so the text-face claim for default_fonts rests on the feature being enabled plus the UIA/state evidence, not on a screenshot.
